about: Every mutant was applied to the file as it is at base_commit, which the change that adds this record does not change. killer is the first test nextest reported failing (it stops at the first failure, with tests running in parallel, so another failing test may be reported first on another run). killer_at says where that test function exists: base, or this_commit for a test the change that adds this record adds. A test that exists at base may still kill only through cases that change adds to it: before_this_change gives the verdict at base where it differs. Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run) before it was called a survivor. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent, and one that is not says why it is not killed yet. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. Every run was on base_commit, with the file and its test module byte for byte as there (or as this change leaves the test module, for survivors_again). The tool's survivors were run again by cargo-mutants itself, selected by an exact --re of their names.

runs.command: each mutant's edits applied as exact text, then cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge -E 'test(/import|numbering|post|approv/)'

cargo build --locked -p bridge-approval-standin --example approval_standin, then every bridge test (-E 'all()'): for the tool's 9 missed mutants as the tool run with --timeout 1800 and an exact --re of their names, after the unmutated tree passed all 5079, and for the 31 hand-written ones the filtered run missed, as the hand run; none was caught there

cargo build --locked -p bridge-approval-standin --example approval_standin, then under -E 'test(/import|numbering|post|approv/)': the tool's 9 as the tool run with --timeout 1800 and an exact --re of their names, after the unmutated tree passed all 2222, and the 31 hand-written ones as the hand run; then for the 5 still missed, every bridge test (-E 'all()', 5094 run), where none was caught

P032.reason: not killed: MAX_KEPT_REFUSALS bounds two things, the kept refusals (keep_refusal) and the batches whose listed box did not fit (note_listed_did_not_fit), so the mutant moves both. Every test that reaches either cap counts to MAX_KEPT_REFUSALS by name (kept_refusals_age_out_and_the_oldest_goes_past_the_cap for the refusals, a_noted_batch_is_asked_again_as_totals_only_for_as_long_as_it_is_remembered for the notes), so a changed cap moves the tests with it. Each number is a size bound on memory with no documented value, not a behaviour a test should pin as a literal

P036.reason: equivalent: a kept refusal's Answered is read only by expired(), which reads its two times, never approved; the flag set here is written and never read

P084.reason: equivalent while the binding is compared whole: a held binding of another kind than the fresh one differs from it in its subject, so binding != *fresh refuses the same redemption with the same code and note

P085.reason: equivalent while voucher_count tells the kinds apart: an approved request's voucher_count is Some only for vouchers and None for masters, as the binding's is, so a request of the other kind than the fresh binding always fails request.voucher_count() != fresh.voucher_count() in the same condition, with the same code and note, in either direction. voucher_count carries the kind only incidentally (post_kind decides it), so a voucher_count that stops telling the kinds apart reopens it, and no test would then fail

P125.reason: equivalent: write_private_file creates no folder, so where the imports folder is missing the open fails and no note is written, as when the check skips the write
